questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Piecewise-Continuous Functions Over Infinite Intervals
questions.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [0,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}-1,\, & ⌊x⌋\text{ is even} \\ 1,\, & ⌊x⌋\text{ is odd},\end{aligned}\,g(x)=u(x-2),\,h(x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡x.
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌊x⌋$ is the floor function.
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $I⊆R.$ A function $f:I\to R$ is piecewise continuous on $I$ if it is piecewise continuous on every closed and bounded subinterval $[a,b]⊂I.$

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=1,2,3,…,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]⊂[0,\infty )$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14064583/assets/084c469b225d2a4cc4bc148fa3a42fb1501141d1adcd91d8d37999409a8d313f.png)

- The function $g(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty )$ since it is continuous over $x\in [0,\infty )$ except at the point $x=2,$ where the one-sided limits exist and are finite:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}g(x)=0,\,{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}g(x)=1
$$

- The function $h(x)$ is not piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ Consider the closed subinterval $x\in [0,2\pi ].$ Notice that the one-sided limits at $x=\pi $ are infinite:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {\pi }^{-}}h(x)=+\infty ,\,{lim}_{x\to {\pi }^{+}}h(x)=-\infty .
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$f$ and $g$ only."

questions.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [0,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)=\sqrt{x+1},\,g(x)={\begin{aligned}1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is even} \\ -1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is odd},\end{aligned}\,h(x)=u(x-1)+u\,(x-\frac{5}{2})+u(x-4).
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌈x⌉$ is the ceiling function.
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $I⊆R.$ A function $f:I\to R$ is piecewise continuous on $I$ if it is piecewise continuous on every closed and bounded subinterval $[a,b]⊂I.$

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ The function is continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$

- The function $g(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=0,1,2,…,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]⊂[0,\infty )$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14064583/assets/d5a497337426dad07096702a3e211f525a959add8cb1fbaaef05fccac26d634b.png)

- The function $h(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty )$ since it is continuous over $x\in [0,\infty )$ except at the points $x=1,$ $x=\frac{5}{2},$ and $x=4,$ where the one-sided limits exist and are finite:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}h(x)=0,\,{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}h(x)=1
$$

$$
{lim}_{x\to 5/{2}^{-}}h(x)=1,\,{lim}_{x\to 5/{2}^{+}}h(x)=2
$$

$$
{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}h(x)=2,\,{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}h(x)=3
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$f,g,$ and $h.$"

questions.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1]?$

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}4x-3, & x<0 \\ -2x+5, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}\,,\,g(x)={x}^{3}-\sqrt[5]{{x}^{3}},\,h(x)={x}^{3}\sqrt[3]{x}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is **piecewise smooth** on $x\in [a,b]$ if

- $f(x)$ is piecewise continuous on $[a,b],$ and

- ${f}^{′}(x)$ exists and is continuous except possibly at finitely many points, where its one-sided limits exist and are finite.

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1].$ We split the interval at $x=0.$ On each open interval, $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1),$ the function is linear. On these intervals,

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}4x-3, & x<0 \\ -2x+5, & x>0\end{aligned}\,,
$$

so

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={\begin{aligned}4, & x<0 \\ -2, & x>0\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $f(x)$ and ${f}^{′}(x)$ are piecewise continuous on each open interval, and they both have finite limits at the endpoints of the subintervals.

- The function $g(x)={x}^{3}-\sqrt[5]{{x}^{3}}$ is not piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1].$ We split the interval at $x=0$ into the two open intervals $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1).$ For $x\ne 0,$

$$
g(x)={x}^{3}-{x}^{3/5},
$$

so

$$
{g}^{′}(x)=3{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{5{x}^{2/5}}.
$$

While this derivative is continuous on the open pieces $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1),$ the limits of the derivative as $x\to 0$ are not finite. In fact, the derivative becomes unbounded near $x=0.$ Thus, the condition for finite limits at the endpoints is not met.

- The function $h(x)={x}^{3}\sqrt[3]{x}$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1].$ Since

$$
h(x)={x}^{10/3},
$$

we have

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{10}{3}{x}^{7/3}.
$$

Here, $h(x)$ and ${h}^{′}(x)$ are continuous on $[-1,1].$ Thus, $h(x)$ is continuously differentiable on the whole interval, and hence piecewise smooth.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$f$ and $h$ only."

questions.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1]?$

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}4x-1, & x<0 \\ 4x+3, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}\,,\,g(x)={x}^{2}+\sqrt[3]{{x}^{4}},\,h(x)={x}^{2}\sqrt[5]{{x}^{4}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is **piecewise smooth** on $x\in [a,b]$ if

- $f(x)$ is piecewise continuous on $[a,b],$ and

- ${f}^{′}(x)$ exists and is continuous except possibly at finitely many points, where its one-sided limits exist and are finite.

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1].$ We split the interval at $x=0.$ On each open interval, $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1),$ the function is linear. On these intervals,

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}4x-1, & x<0 \\ 4x+3, & x>0\end{aligned}\,,
$$

so

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={\begin{aligned}4, & x<0 \\ 4, & x>0\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $f(x)$ and ${f}^{′}(x)$ are piecewise continuous on each open interval, and they both have finite limits at the endpoints of the subintervals.

- The function $g(x)={x}^{2}+\sqrt[3]{{x}^{4}}$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1].$ Since

$$
g(x)={x}^{2}+\sqrt[3]{{x}^{4}}={x}^{2}+{x}^{4/3},
$$

we have

$$
{g}^{′}(x)=2x+\frac{4}{3}{x}^{1/3}.
$$

Here, $g(x)$ and ${g}^{′}(x)$ are continuous on $[-1,1].$ Thus, $g(x)$ is continuously differentiable on the whole interval, and hence piecewise smooth.

- The function $h(x)={x}^{2}\sqrt[5]{{x}^{4}}$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1].$ Since

$$
h(x)={x}^{2}\sqrt[5]{{x}^{4}}={x}^{14/5},
$$

we have

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{14}{5}{x}^{9/5}.
$$

Here, $h(x)$ and ${h}^{′}(x)$ are continuous on $[-1,1].$ Thus, $h(x)$ is continuously differentiable on the whole interval, and hence piecewise smooth.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$f,$ $g,$ and $h.$"
